title: Storms May Slow Thanksgiving Trips
summary: Thanksgiving is one of the busiest travel weeks of the year. This year, storms may make trips harder. Storms on both coasts could delay flights and car trips as families travel for the holiday. On Monday, more than 3,700 flights were delayed. Chicago's O'Hare Airport had a ground stop, so planes waited on the ground instead of taking off. Airlines are also still fixing problems from recent computer failures. Delta, a very big airline, says its flights are running again after a computer system went down. But delays from that problem are still causing trouble. On the West Coast, storms from the Pacific Ocean are expected to bring heavy rain and snow in the mountains. In the East, a storm forming over the Gulf of Mexico could bring rain, strong winds, and snow. Florida may see more rain after a week of heavy rain that already caused flooding. Millions of people fly or drive to see family for Thanksgiving. Even a small delay can mean long lines at the airport. If your family is traveling this week, check your flight before you leave home.
why_it_matters: If your family is traveling for Thanksgiving, a storm delay could mean waiting in long lines at the airport.
